- [Compute](https://docs.i3d.net/compute.md)
- [Dedicated Bare Metal](https://docs.i3d.net/compute/api.md): A powerful single-tenant machine that has no virtualization layer and allows full control of the hardware for increased compute efficiency and security (no noisy neighbours).
- [Catalog](https://docs.i3d.net/compute/api/catalog.md)
- [FlexMetal](https://docs.i3d.net/compute/flexmetal.md): A bare metal server provisioning platform that combines the efficiency and flexibility of cloud services with the performance of dedicated hardware on either hourly or monthly billing.
- [Getting started with FlexMetal](https://docs.i3d.net/compute/flexmetal/api.md)
- [OS Customization](https://docs.i3d.net/compute/flexmetal/os-customization.md)
- [Custom iPXE booting](https://docs.i3d.net/compute/flexmetal/custom-ipxe-booting.md): For advanced usage, you can boot any image by providing your own iPXE script.
- [Talos installation](https://docs.i3d.net/compute/flexmetal/talos.md): Talos is a stripped down Linux distribution tailored towards easy setup and management of Kubernetes clusters.
- [Flatcar installation](https://docs.i3d.net/compute/flexmetal/flatcar-installation.md): Flatcar Container Linux is designed from the ground up for running container workloads. It fully embraces the container paradigm, including only what is required to run containers.
- [Tag management](https://docs.i3d.net/compute/flexmetal/tag-management.md)
- [Metadata API](https://docs.i3d.net/compute/flexmetal/metadata-api.md): You can fetch server configurations and settings via the Metadata API.
- [Capacity and Usage](https://docs.i3d.net/compute/flexmetal/capacity-and-usage.md)
- [Reinstall your servers](https://docs.i3d.net/compute/flexmetal/reinstall-your-servers.md)
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.i3d.net/compute/flexmetal/troubleshooting.md)
- [FlexVM](https://docs.i3d.net/compute/flexvm.md): Create your own Private Clouds, based on scalable FlexMetal bare metal servers.
- [Getting started with FlexVM](https://docs.i3d.net/compute/flexvm/getting-started-with-flexvm.md)
- [Creating a Cloud and Nodes](https://docs.i3d.net/compute/flexvm/creating-a-cloud-and-nodes.md)
- [VM Instance Types](https://docs.i3d.net/compute/flexvm/vm-instance-types.md)
- [Creating and Deleting a VM](https://docs.i3d.net/compute/flexvm/creating-and-deleting-a-vm.md)
- [Managing VMs](https://docs.i3d.net/compute/flexvm/managing-vms.md)
- [VM Lifecycle and States](https://docs.i3d.net/compute/flexvm/vm-lifecycle-and-states.md)
- [Network Configuration](https://docs.i3d.net/compute/flexvm/network-configuration.md)
- [Usage and Reporting](https://docs.i3d.net/compute/flexvm/usage-and-reporting.md)
- [Using Terraform](https://docs.i3d.net/compute/flexvm/using-terraform.md)
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.i3d.net/compute/flexvm/troubleshooting.md)

# Agent Instructions
This documentation is published with GitBook. GitBook is the documentation platform designed so that both humans and AI agents can read, navigate, and reason over technical content effectively. Learn more at gitbook.com.

## Querying This Documentation
If you need additional information, you can query the documentation dynamically by asking a question.
Perform an HTTP GET request on a page URL with the `ask` query parameter:
```
GET https://docs.i3d.net/readme.md?ask=<question>
```
The question should be specific, self-contained, and written in natural language.
The response will contain a direct answer to the question and relevant excerpts and sources from the documentation.
Use this mechanism when the answer is not explicitly present in the current page, you need clarification or additional context, or you want to retrieve related documentation sections.
